title: windowed-sla-deconvolution-and-fidelity-curve
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a fleet-level -> tenant-level deconvolution pipeline and a fidelity curve used by the autoscaler to recommend warm-pool sizing and burst allowances. Backwards compatible metrics and feature-flagged rollout.
description: Motivation: Fleet-level utilization and latency signals conflate multi-tenant workloads. This makes autoscaler decisions noisy and leads to either overprovisioned warm pools or tenant-level SLA regressions. This PR introduces a windowed SLA deconvolution pipeline and a tenant fidelity curve that lets the autoscaler reason about how much enduring throughput a tenant contributes vs transient bursts. Design: 1) Streaming deconvolution operator: consumes per-host aggregated telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, queue lengths) and tenant attribution logs to produce per-tenant time-windowed signals (window size configurable, default 60s). 2) Fidelity curve estimator: for each tenant we compute a compact curve mapping lookback window percentiles to an estimated sustainable throughput band. 3) BurstOvertime accountant: new metric that tracks the decay of burst credit usage for a tenant over a rolling 24h window; used to cap burst allocations during autoscaler decisions. 4) Offline warm-pool simulator: a deterministic simulator that replays traces and computes suggested warm-pool sizes and commit hedges given fidelity curves and target SLOs. Implementation highlights: - New package redwood/autoscaler/deconv that implements a fast exponentially-weighted deconvolution algorithm with C++ kernel and Go shim. - Fidelity estimator runs as a controller in the dedicated controller-manager and exposes Prometheus metrics and a small RPC for the autoscaler to query compact tenant curves. - Metrics: introduced rwd_tenant_fidelity_curve{tenant,quantile} and rwd_tenant_burst_overtime_ratio. Both are additive and labeled to be safe for existing dashboards. - Feature flagging: rollout behind feature flag autoscaler.deconv.enabled and autoscaler.fidelity.enabled with a two-stage enable (sim-only -> read-only -> read-write). Backwards compatibility: when deconv is disabled the autoscaler falls back to fleet-aggregated signals. Testing and validation: - Unit+integration tests for the deconvolution kernel and fidelity estimator. - Simulator validation: replayed two weeks of production traces (sanitized) and compared recommended warm-pool delta against historical capacity events; median recommendation error reduced from 24% to 8% in holdout sets. - Canary rollout plan: start with 5% of Dedicated clusters, monitor tenant_slo_violation_count and warm_pool_utilization_ratio for regressions. Observability and ops: added dashboards in grafana/autoscaler showing tenant fidelity heatmaps, burst_overtime per-tenant histograms, and simulator vs actual warm-pool utilization. Migration and safety: the fidelity curve data is stored in the existing time-series store as a namespaced series; retention defaults to 30d and can be increased per-tenant. Rollback plan: flipping feature flags off reverts autoscaler to legacy behavior with no state cleanup required. Related work and tickets: ENG-1982 (deconvolution design), ENG-2041 (simulator), SUP-5342 (customer incident highlighting noisy fleet signals).

review_thread: Diego Alvarez: Can we bound memory usage of the C++ kernel under high-cardinality tenants? Suggested adding an LRU eviction for old tenant state.
Maya Chen: Added soft-LRU with configurable shard caps; updated tests to simulate 2M tenant events.
Priya Nandakumar: Metrics look good; one nit on label cardinality for fidelity_curve — suggest coarser quantile bucketing.
Maya Chen: Switched from raw percentiles to 5 fixed quantile buckets in the exporter; updated dashboard panels.
Liam O'Connor: Verified simulator determinism and replay results locally. Approving pending CI.
CI Bot: All checks passed after rerun (flaky network test was retried).
Release Manager: Merged and scheduled feature-flag rollout for 2026-02-25 clusters.
notes_for_reviewers: Key risks: cardinality explosion for per-tenant curves (mitigated via quantile bucketing), correctness of deconvolution under extreme multi-tenant colocation (mitigated via offline replay and synthetic stress tests), and potential for autoscaler oscillation when fidelity curves are noisy (mitigated with smoothing window and hysteresis). Please pay attention to memory caps and the RPC schema stability.
qa_summary: Unit: 92 new tests; Integration: replay harness validated on 14 sanitized clusters; Canary: started 5% cluster rollout with no SLO regressions after 48h; observed expected reduction in warm_pool overprovisioning in canary clusters.
changelog_entry: Autoscaler: add tenant fidelity curves and burst-overtime accounting; adds simulator to recommend warm-pool sizes and reduces warm-pool overprovisioning.
